paper_metadata.title: Major Bleeding and Thromboembolic Events in Veno-Venous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation-Patients With Isolated Respiratory Failure

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a very clear description of the target population (isolated respiratory failure) and uses a rigorous flowchart to show how the final sample was derived from a larger registry. Inclusion/exclusion criteria are explicit and clinical characteristics are well-defined.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: This analysis included all adult patients (≥ 18 years) requiring vvECMO for severe respiratory failure (PaO2/FiO2 < 85 mmHg or refractory respiratory acidosis with pH < 7.25 on optimized positive end-expiratory pressure, usually ≥ 15 mm Hg)
items.reasoning: The authors define the specific clinical parameters (PaO2/FiO2, pH, PEEP) that characterize the population of interest.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Patient data have been derived from the Regensburg ECMO-Registry.
items.reasoning: The use of a comprehensive institutional registry (Regensburg ECMO-Registry) for a specific time period is clearly stated.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: from March 2009 to October 2017
items.reasoning: The start and end dates are explicitly provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: at the University Hospital Regensburg, Germany.
items.reasoning: The specific tertiary care center and location are identified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Exclusion criteria for this analysis predisposing for bleeding and thromboembolic were defined as: Hepatic impairment... Kidney-failure... Patients suffering from polytrauma... Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia...
items.reasoning: The study lists specific clinical and laboratory-based exclusion criteria to isolate the population of interest.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Of 601 patients, 123 patients... were eligible for the analysis.
items.reasoning: The flowchart (Figure 1) accounts for all patients in the registry, ensuring no unexplained exclusions.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The mean age and days on ECMO were similar in both groups... isolated respiratory failure cohort had a lower body mass index... fewer male patients... Lower Sepsis-related Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score at baseline
items.reasoning: Key demographics and clinical severity scores (SOFA) are reported for the study sample.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: As a retrospective registry-based study of ICU patients, the 'follow-up' is the duration of the ECMO run/hospital stay. The study accounts for almost all patients for the primary outcomes, though there is a slight drop-off in thromboembolic evaluation (92%) which is explained by the timing of the diagnostic test (post-decannulation).

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Of 123 included patients, 113 (92%) have been evaluated for the occurrence of thromboembolic events as defined.
items.reasoning: 92% completion for the thromboembolic outcome is high; 100% appear to have been assessed for bleeding.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The text does not explicitly describe attempts to follow up on the 10 patients missing thromboembolic data, likely because they died before decannulation.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: routine duplex sonography was conducted after decannulation, thus affecting our rates of thromboembolism in those surviving and nonsurviving.
items.reasoning: The authors acknowledge that the 8% missing data for thromboembolism is due to the timing of the test relative to death/decannulation.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There is no specific table comparing the characteristics of the 10 patients missing thromboembolic data vs. the 113 analyzed.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: the rate of thromboembolic events in deceased patients must be considered underreported
items.reasoning: The authors admit a potential systematic difference (survivors vs. non-survivors) in who received the thromboembolic assessment.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (laboratory values like aPTT, Platelets, PaCO2) are measured using standardized, automated laboratory equipment. The methods are consistent for all patients.

items.reasoning: The prognostic factors are standard clinical laboratory parameters.

items.reasoning: Standardized commercial assays and automated analyzers were used, ensuring high reliability.

items.reasoning: A uniform protocol was applied to all patients in the ICU setting.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While bleeding definitions are standardized (ELSO), the thromboembolic outcome measurement is subject to bias because duplex sonography was performed after decannulation, potentially missing events in patients who died on ECMO.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Major bleeding events were defined following the recommendations of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization anticoagulation guidelines... Thromboembolic events were assessed by duplex sonography within 3 days after decannulation or CT scan
items.reasoning: The study uses established international guidelines (ELSO, Schulman et al.) for bleeding and specific imaging criteria for thrombosis.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Duplex sonography was performed by specially trained physicians. Diagnosis was based on incompressibility of the vein, absence of flow, and presence of thrombus.
items.reasoning: While the imaging method is valid, there is no mention of blinding the assessors to the prognostic factors (e.g., aPTT levels).

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.reasoning: The protocol for daily bleeding assessment and post-decannulation ultrasound was standardized.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study attempts to control for confounding by selecting a very specific 'isolated respiratory failure' cohort (design-based control). However, the multivariable analysis is limited, and some clinical factors (like platelet function or anti-Xa) were not measured.

items.reasoning: Basic confounders were measured, but the authors admit that anti-Xa and platelet function were not.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods are appropriate for the data types. The authors provide a clear account of their analytical strategy, including how they handled the temporal relationship between aPTT and bleeding (analyzing aPTT *until* the event).
